name: Centro Storico
tagline: Inside the walls, with the mosaics a few minutes apart
description: The historic centre around Piazza del Popolo, where San Vitale, Galla Placidia, the Neonian baptistery and Dante's tomb all sit within a short walk of each other. Largely pedestrianised, flat and small enough to cross in fifteen minutes, with the market, the cafes and the restaurants all inside it.
bestFor: Anyone who wants eight UNESCO buildings and the market on the same walk
pros: The mosaics, the market and the restaurants all within ten minutes
Pedestrianised and completely flat for cycling
Train station a few minutes on foot
cons: The highest rents in the town
Visitor traffic around the main monuments

name: Borgo San Rocco and the Western Districts
tagline: Just outside the walls, residential and better value
description: The residential streets immediately west of the centre, a mix of interwar houses and post-war apartment buildings with local shops, schools and a normal Italian neighbourhood pace. It is a ten-minute cycle to Piazza del Popolo and rents drop noticeably as soon as you cross the ring road.
bestFor: Longer stays that want a normal neighbourhood and a short cycle in
pros: Ten minutes by bike to the mosaics
Everyday shops and a local market
cons: Ring road traffic on the eastern edge

name: Classe
tagline: The old port site, with Sant'Apollinare and the pinewood
description: Five kilometres south of the centre, where the Roman fleet's harbour once stood and where Sant'Apollinare in Classe, the finest of the mosaic basilicas, sits alone in the fields. The historic pinewood runs beside it towards the sea. Quiet, green and connected to town by train and cycle path.
bestFor: Stays that want the pinewood and the basilica rather than a town centre
pros: Sant'Apollinare and the archaeological park on the doorstep
Historic pinewood for running and cycling
Direct train and a flat cycle route to the centre
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes from the town
Mosquitoes from the pinewood in summer

name: Marina di Ravenna
tagline: The town's beach, twelve kilometres out with the summer season
description: Ravenna's seaside district on the Adriatic, with a long sand beach, the beach clubs that run the summer, a marina and a pinewood behind. In July and August it is where the town's evening life relocates; from October it is largely shut. Bus and cycle path connect it to the centre.
bestFor: Summer stays that want the beach and the seasonal nightlife
pros: Long sand beach and the summer beach clubs
Marina, pinewood and cycle path to town
Where the evening actually happens in season
cons: Almost entirely shut from October to April
Twenty-five minutes to the centre by bus
Industrial port immediately to the south

name: Darsena and the Canal District
tagline: The old dock, slowly being converted
description: The strip of canal and warehouses running from behind the station towards the port, an industrial area under long-running redevelopment with some converted buildings, event spaces and newer apartments. It is the closest thing Ravenna has to a changing neighbourhood, and rents reflect that it is not finished.
bestFor: People who want newer flats near the station at below-centre prices
pros: Two minutes from the station and the centre
Event spaces and summer programming on the water
